Read off each paper's LaTeX (papers/.cache/<id>.tex) on 26 Oct 2026 by four Claude agents that saw only the LaTeX and the protocol below, never an extraction; every quote is verbatim in the source and every number inside its quote (checked by script). configs: every size configuration of the paper's own models the paper states; a field the paper does not state is null. structure: norm_placement (pre, post, sandwich, or per sublayer {attn, ffn} with branch_post = the norm on the sublayer's output inside the residual branch), parallel_block, ffn_gated; null = not stated. A label changes only when the source shows it wrong, never to make an extractor pass. new_fields (27 Oct 2026, one Claude agent under the same rule: LaTeX only, no extraction): qk_norm (per_head, full, unspecified, none, or absent = never mentioned), ssm (mamba1, s4, absent; with d_state, d_conv, expand, dt_rank), new_ops (elementwise or row ops outside the standard set, with each input's role and a learned input's init; category and scored added on merge), token_mixing_ops (listed, not scored), and positional for the 11 papers flavor_bench.TRUTH leaves unlabelled (with T5's rel_buckets and rel_max_distance).
protocol:
Truth labels for the arXiv extractor's benchmark: sizes and block structure, read off the LaTeX.

Source: the paper's LaTeX, cached at
  C:\Users\jonat\OneDrive\Documents\research_portfolio_complete\microtorch\papers\.cache\<arxiv_id>.tex
Read ONLY that file for each paper (Grep and Read with offsets; some files are large). Do NOT open anything
under microtorch\papers\llm_extract_receipts, microtorch\experiments, microtorch\papers\.cache\llm, or any
*.extraction.json: the labels must be independent of the extractor being scored. Do not use your own memory
of the model: a value the LaTeX does not state is null, even if you "know" it.

For each paper, label what the paper states about ITS OWN model(s) (not baselines, not related work, not
models it only compares against, not rejected ablations, not future work).

1. configs: every size configuration of the paper's own models that the paper states (usually a table:
   one row per model size). For each config give:
     name            the paper's name for it (e.g. "7B", "BERT-base", "125M")
     d_model         hidden width
     n_layers        number of layers (blocks). For encoder-decoder models: layers per stack, and say so in notes.
     n_heads         attention (query) heads
     n_kv_heads      key/value heads, ONLY when the paper states grouped-query / multi-query (else null)
     d_ff            FFN inner width
     vocab_size      vocabulary size, when stated for the model (a global statement applies to every config)
     context_length  the model's training context / sequence length, when stated (a global statement applies to every config)
   Each field: {"value": <number>, "quote": "<verbatim span from the LaTeX that contains the number>"} or null.
   A quote is ONE contiguous span copied character for character from the .tex (LaTeX commands, &, $ and all),
   e.g. a table row "6.7B & 32 & 4096 & 32 & 128". Numbers as plain integers (4K -> 4096 only if the paper
   means 4096; "2048" stays 2048). If the paper gives head_dim and heads but not d_model, do not compute
   d_model: null.
2. structure (each {"value": ..., "quote": "<verbatim span>"} or null when the paper does not state it):
     norm_placement  "pre" (each sublayer's input is normalised: x + f(norm(x))), "post" (norm after the
                     residual add: norm(x + f(x))), "sandwich" (norm on the sublayer's input and output),
                     or "other:<short description>" (e.g. different per sublayer). An explicit statement
                     that the model follows a named model's placement counts only if it names the
                     placement ("pre-normalization as in GPT-2").
     parallel_block  true when attention and FFN run in parallel on the same input ("parallel
                     formulation", y = x + attn(ln(x)) + mlp(ln(x))), false only when the paper says so
                     explicitly or its equations/figure show the sequential block; else null.
     ffn_gated       true when the FFN is a gated linear unit (SwiGLU, GeGLU, ReGLU, GLU, "gated-GELU"),
                     false when the paper states a plain two-matrix FFN (ReLU/GeLU between two linears).
3. notes: one or two sentences: which model you took as the paper's own, anything ambiguous.

Write ONE JSON file (UTF-8, valid JSON, no comments): a list of objects
  {"arxiv_id": "...", "model": "...", "configs": [...], "structure": {"norm_placement": ..., "parallel_block": ...,
   "ffn_gated": ...}, "notes": "..."}
in the order you were given the ids. Before writing, re-check that every quote occurs verbatim in that paper's
.tex (use Grep with a distinctive fixed substring of the quote) and that each number occurs inside its quote.
